newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Marcopper ex-officials deny waste charges.
newsitem.headline: Marcopper ex-officials deny waste charges.

text.p: Two Australian former executives of Marcopper Mining Corp and a Filipino manager on Wednesday pleaded not guilty to charges of causing property damage after mine waste swamped a Philippine river.

A court clerk read the charges against former Marcopper president and chief executive John Loney, ex-resident manager Steven Reid and senior manager Pedro Hernandez at the start of hearings before a judge in Boac town on Marinduque island, 160 km (100 miles) south of Manila.
Marcopper's copper ore mill in Marinduque has been closed since March last year after waste from a storage reservoir swamped the 25 km (15 mile) Boac river.
Loney and Reid have since resigned from Marcopper. They were nominees of Canada's Placer Dome Inc which earlier this year pulled out of its 39.9 percent stake in the Philippine firm.
The three executives were charged with reckless imprudence resulting in damage to property and violation of the mining law.
A lawyer for the three entered a not guilty plea for them on the reckless imprudence charge.
The defendants have asked for the dismissal of the mining law violation charge and refused to enter a plea. Automatically, the court entered a "not guilty" plea for them.
Placer officials said in Manila last week Placer would spend between $70 million and $75 million to clean up the Boac river and compensate locals.
